_README: Which committee each card belongs to. EDIT THIS FILE, not Python.
A purchase on a verified card that is in its cohort's dates is booked to
that card's committee outright, ahead of every other rule (treasury ruling,
2026-09-23). Getting this file right matters more than anything else in
categorization.
Add a card by copying a block below and filling it in. The key is the last
four digits as they appear in the bank description ('... CARD 0594').
committee : the committee ID. The reference table is on the Treasury page,
or in ais_fmd/config/categories.py.
holder    : whose card it is. Shown to a treasurer as part of the reason.
verified  : true  = treasury has confirmed this in writing. Decides the row.
false = inferred or assumed. A weak hint only, labelled
'unconfirmed' wherever it is used.
socials_to: optional. A committee ID for socials (bars, liquor stores)
bought on this card, when they belong somewhere other than
the card's committee.
era       : the officer cohort this was confirmed under -- a name from
_eras below. The card only applies to transactions dated
inside that cohort's start/end, so a new cohort's cards replace
the old ones instead of both voting.
NEW OFFICER COHORT: add its window to _eras, point _current_era at it, and
add the new cards with that era. Leave the old cohort's cards in place --
they still categorize that cohort's statements correctly.
A card that is not listed here contributes NO signal at all. That is
deliberate -- guessing a cardholder is how spending gets booked against the
wrong committee's budget silently.
Keys beginning with an underscore are ignored.
